cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Let's make this chess game decide who cooks all weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were playing for a biscuit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Neither of us has been emotionally changed by the biscuit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't need chess to change me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll enjoy discovering how much the kitchen matters.

mechanism: A treats its chess pupil biscuit stake as childish practice, pressing for a weekend cooking penalty to make the result alter something real.
confusable: Not merely asking for another game: A wants a larger specific commitment because a low-cost result leaves both players unaffected.
comparison: Household cooking burden versus public captaincy status.
seedUse: D200 chess/biscuit/weekend cooking/change; S05 taught beginner stakes.
